title: By the sky with its great stars.
subtitle: An oath to open a surah of comfort
then: This surah came when {trap}persecution in Makkah was at its height{/trap}. Ibn Abbas and others said the Buruj are the stars; Ibn Jarir said the twelve positions the sun and moon travel through. {idea}An ordered sky opens a surah meant to console.{/idea}
now: Your life feels out of control: the diagnosis, the layoff, the family fight. {reward}Step outside at night.{/reward} The stars are still on their exact paths, held by the One who holds you.
old: When my life falls apart, it feels like nobody is in charge.
new: The Lord who keeps the stars in order is in charge of my hardship too.
try: Look at the night sky tonight for one minute and hand one worry to Allah.

title: And by the Promised Day.
subtitle: A day on the calendar that will come
then: The hadith from Abu Hurayrah cited by Ibn Kathir says the Promised Day is {idea}the Day of Judgement{/idea}. To believers being persecuted in Makkah, this was a promise that their suffering had a court date.
now: You were cheated by someone who will never be caught. Your complaint went nowhere. {reward}The verse says there is a Day already promised for exactly this.{/reward}
old: Some wrongs will just never be put right.
new: Every unsettled wrong has a promised Day.
try: Leave one wrong done to you with Allah today, and stop replaying it.

title: And by the witness and what is witnessed.
subtitle: Days that see and days that are seen
then: A hadith cited by Ibn Kathir says the witness is {idea}Friday{/idea} and the witnessed is {idea}the day of Arafah{/idea}. It says Friday holds an hour in which a Muslim who asks Allah for good is given it. Others said the witnessed is the Day of Judgement.
now: Friday arrives as another busy workday, lunch rushed, phone buzzing. {reward}There is an hour in it where your dua is answered.{/reward}
old: Friday is just another day with a prayer in the middle.
new: Friday is a witness day with an hour of answered prayer hidden in it.
try: This Friday, set aside five minutes in the late afternoon just for dua.

title: Cursed were the people of the ditch.
subtitle: The story the oaths were leading to
then: Ibn Kathir relates the hadith of the boy and the king from Muslim: a boy's faith led a whole crowd to say {reward}we believe in the Lord of the boy{/reward}. The king had ditches dug and fires lit for anyone who would not give up faith.
now: You may never face fire, but you will face pressure: the joke at work about your prayer, the friend who says faith is old-fashioned. {idea}The story asks what you will hold on to.{/idea}
old: The ones with the power always come out on top.
new: Those who torment believers are the ones who truly lose.
try: Stand firm on one small part of your faith today when it would be easier to drop it.

title: A fire kept fed with fuel.
subtitle: Cruelty that was planned and maintained
then: Ibn Kathir says they dug a ditch, {trap}lit a fire in it and prepared fuel to keep it ablaze{/trap}, then asked the believers again to give up their faith. The believers still refused.
now: A grudge kept burning for years, fed with screenshots, old stories, and new complaints. {idea}Cruelty rarely stays alive on its own. Someone keeps feeding it.{/idea}
old: Harm that lasts just sort of happens.
new: Lasting harm is kept going by someone choosing to feed it.
try: Stop adding fuel to one conflict today: do not repeat the story.

title: They sat around it.
subtitle: Comfortable beside someone else's suffering
then: The verse pictures the persecutors seated at the edge of the ditch. {trap}They were not rushed or ashamed. They sat.{/trap} The surah introduction ties this to the Makkan chiefs who were also pressuring believers.
now: Someone is being humiliated in the group chat and you just watch, reading every message. {idea}Sitting comfortably beside harm is not neutral.{/idea}
old: If I am only watching, I am not part of it.
new: Sitting at ease while someone is hurt is a stance, not nothing.
try: Next time you see someone mocked today, say one kind word for them or leave.

title: They watched what they were doing to the believers.
subtitle: Witnesses to their own crime
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}were witnesses to what was done to these believers{/trap}. They could not claim later they did not know. And the surah adds that Allah too is Witness over everything.
now: You saw the colleague being pushed out unfairly. You saw the sibling left out of the inheritance talk. {idea}Seeing it makes you part of the record.{/idea}
old: I did not do it. I only saw it.
new: What I see clearly, I will be asked about.
try: Think of one unfairness you have watched quietly. Take one small step to help.

title: Their only crime was believing in the Mighty, the Praised.
subtitle: When faith itself is the accusation
then: Ibn Kathir says these believers committed no sin in their persecutors' eyes {trap}except their faith in Allah{/trap}. He adds that Allah is Mighty and Praiseworthy in all He decrees, {idea}even when the reason is unknown to many people{/idea}.
now: You are passed over for the team trip because you do not drink, or teased for fasting at school. {reward}If faith is the only thing they hold against you, you are in good company.{/reward}
old: If people hold my faith against me, I should hide it.
new: Being disliked only for believing is something to be proud of, not hide.
try: Thank Allah today for one way your faith makes you stand out.

title: His is the kingdom of heaven and earth, and He sees everything.
subtitle: The real owner of the ground they ruled

row.title: the king
sub: owned a ditch and an army

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah owns the heavens, the earth, and all between them, and {idea}nothing is concealed from Him{/idea}. The king seemed to own everything. The verse names the real Owner.
now: The manager who decides your contract, the landlord with your deposit. {trap}They seem to hold everything.{/trap} {reward}The verse reminds you who actually owns it all, and that He saw what they did.{/reward}
old: The person with power over me has the final say.
new: Allah owns everything, and sees how power is used over me.
try: Before a meeting with someone who has power over you, say: Allah is the real Owner.

title: Those who torment believers, then never repent, face the Fire.
subtitle: Even here, the door of repentance is named
then: Ibn Abbas and others said tormented here means they burned them. Yet Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: {reward}look at this generosity. They killed Allah's friends, and He still invites them to repent.{/reward}
now: You have hurt someone badly, maybe someone who was only trying to do right. {reward}If even the people of the ditch were offered repentance, the door is open for you.{/reward} Walk through it today.
old: What I did is too serious to be forgiven.
new: Allah invites even the worst wrongdoers back. The condition is only that I return.
try: Apologise to one person you have wronged, or ask Allah's forgiveness for it tonight.
